chunks: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله entered upon a man from Banī Hāshim while he was in the throes of death, and he said to him: “Say: There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. There is no god but Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the seven heavens, and Lord of the seven earths, and whatever is in them, and whatever is between them, and whatever is beneath them, and Lord of the Mighty Throne.
And peace be upon the messengers, and all praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.”
So he said it, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “All praise belongs to Allah who rescued him from the Fire.”

key_terms.النَّزْعِ: the throes of death or final moments before dying
key_terms.الْحَلِيمُ: the Forbearing, one of Allah’s attributes indicating restraint and clemency
key_terms.الْكَرِيمُ: the Generous, one of Allah’s attributes indicating nobility and bounty
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ: glory be to Allah; a formula of declaring Allah’s transcendence
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: the declaration of divine oneness and exclusive worship of Allah

ai.seo_question: What should be recited to a dying person according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله instructed a dying man from Banī Hāshim to recite a declaration of tawhid, glorification of Allah, and a Qur'anic ending of peace upon the messengers and praise of Allah. After the man recited it, the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله said that Allah had saved him from the Fire, showing the salvific importance of this remembrance at the time of death.
